scientific_question: Can two independent camera-member event rates at a common site identify diel ecological activity separately from a common diel effective-detection factor?

conditional_model.observations: E[Y_j(t)]= effort_j(t) * lambda(t) * p_j(t), for j=1,2
assumptions: effort_j(t) is known from deployment records
lambda(t) is latent ecological encounter/activity intensity
p_j(t) is camera-specific effective detection and may vary by time
camera members retain separate identities but do not observe labeled common passage events
conditional_model.gauge_witness: For any positive nonconstant h(t) with p_j(t)/h(t) <= 1, lambda'(t)=h(t)lambda(t), p_j'(t)=p_j(t)/h(t) leaves both expected rates unchanged
conditional_model.uniquely_recoverable_under_equal_exposur: relative p1(t)/p2(t) may be inferred under a COMMON encounter intensity, not the absolute detection probabilities or common diel factor
conditional_model.two_cameras_50_100m_apart_additional_ris: different camera microsites may have different local lambda_j(t), so even relative p1/p2 is confounded with unequal activity in their fields of view

escape_routes_that_must_be_verified_befo: paired co-detection of identified same animal passages from jointly observed fields, with independently justified conditional-detection assumptions
external calibrated passage counts or another detection/distance calibration channel indexed by physical camera deployments
a separately justified repeated-visit observation model which proves diel activity-detection identification and is not just site occupancy detection
what_this_does_not_prove: the published Rhode Island field study is invalid
relative source-camera detection can never be estimated
candidate_decision: G4 REMAINS UNPASSED; ZIP headers alone cannot pass G4, even if camera IDs exist
